title: Cache

## Overview

`github.com/xraph/forge/extensions/cache` gives your app a key-value cache with per-key TTLs, a default
expiry, key prefixes, glob-style key lookup and size limits. It registers the cache in the DI
container so any service can ask for it.

The in-memory driver is the one that works today. The config also accepts `redis` and `memcached`,
but those drivers aren't implemented yet: config validation passes, then building the service fails
with "redis driver not yet implemented" (or the memcached equivalent), so the app doesn't start.

## What It Registers

| Service | How you resolve it | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Cache service | `forge.Inject[*cache.CacheService]`, or the name `cache` | `*CacheService` |
| Cache interface | `forge.Inject[cache.Cache]`, `cache.GetCache` | `Cache`, backed by the same `*CacheService` singleton |

The extension's `Start` resolves the service and connects the backend. Its `Stop` disconnects it,
which empties the in-memory store.

## Quick Start

You need Go 1.26 or later. Add the modules:

```bash
go get github.com/xraph/forge@latest
go get github.com/xraph/forge/extensions/cache@latest
```

Save this as `main.go`:

```go
package main

import (
	"errors"
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"time"

	"github.com/xraph/forge"
	"github.com/xraph/forge/extensions/cache"
)

func main() {
	app := forge.NewApp(forge.AppConfig{
		Name:        "cache-demo",
		HTTPAddress: ":8080",
		Extensions: []forge.Extension{
			cache.NewExtension(
				cache.WithDefaultTTL(10*time.Minute),
				cache.WithPrefix("demo:"),
			),
		},
	})

	err := app.Router().GET("/greeting", func(ctx forge.Context) error {
		c, err := cache.GetCache(app.Container())
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}

		value, err := c.Get(ctx.Context(), "greeting")
		if errors.Is(err, cache.ErrNotFound) {
			value = []byte("Hello from the cache")
			if err := c.Set(ctx.Context(), "greeting", value, 30*time.Second); err != nil {
				return err
			}

			return ctx.JSON(http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"source": "miss", "value": string(value)})
		}
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}

		return ctx.JSON(http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"source": "hit", "value": string(value)})
	})
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}

	if err := app.Run(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

Run it and call the route twice:

```bash
go mod tidy
go run .

curl http://localhost:8080/greeting
# {"source":"miss","value":"Hello from the cache"}
curl http://localhost:8080/greeting
# {"source":"hit","value":"Hello from the cache"}
```

The second call comes from memory. Thirty seconds later you get a miss again, because the handler
wrote the key with its own 30-second TTL, and that wins over the ten-minute default you set on the
extension.

## Using Cache in Your Services

Take `cache.Cache` as a constructor parameter and the container fills it in:

```go
type SessionStore struct {
	cache cache.Cache
}

func NewSessionStore(c cache.Cache) *SessionStore {
	return &SessionStore{cache: c}
}

func (s *SessionStore) Save(ctx context.Context, sessionID string, data []byte) error {
	return s.cache.Set(ctx, "session:"+sessionID, data, 30*time.Minute)
}

func (s *SessionStore) Load(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) ([]byte, error) {
	return s.cache.Get(ctx, "session:"+sessionID)
}
```

Register the constructor after `forge.NewApp`:

```go
err := forge.Provide(app.Container(), NewSessionStore)
```

If you'd rather pull the cache out yourself, `cache.GetCache(container)`, `cache.GetCacheFromApp(app)`
and `forge.Inject[cache.Cache](container)` all return the same singleton.

## Key Concepts

- Drivers: `inmemory` works. `redis` and `memcached` pass validation and then fail at service
  construction. The in-memory driver sweeps expired entries in the background and, when it's full,
  evicts one entry per `Set` (an expired one if it finds one, otherwise an arbitrary one). That is
  not LRU.
- Key prefixing: `Prefix` is added to every key on write and stripped from `Keys` results.
- TTL defaults: a `Set` with `ttl == 0` uses `DefaultTTL`.
- Extra interfaces: the in-memory backend also implements `StringCache` and `JSONCache`.
  `CounterCache` and `MultiCache` are declared in the package, but nothing implements them yet.

## Important Runtime Notes

- `CacheService.Health` pings the backend. The extension's own `Health` only reports whether it has
  started.
- The in-memory backend records counters named `cache_hit`, `cache_miss`, `cache_set`,
  `cache_delete`, `cache_clear` and `cache_evict` through Forge metrics.
- `Keys()` takes a glob with at most one `*`. A pattern with two wildcards matches nothing.
- YAML keys are snake_case (`default_ttl`, `max_size`). The old Go field names still apply with a
  warning. See [Configuration](/docs/extensions/cache/configuration).
